This is conclusion-blind relative to selected candidate fields, not independent proposal generation: call B depends on call A's premise extraction and topology. The visible dependency is recorded, and no independence confidence bonus is assigned.
At most four seams from a 24-node/48-edge DAG; checker equivalence and substitution remain restricted to an admitted fragment.
nodes.hypothesis: At equal budget, masked seam reconstruction exposes more unsupported interface steps than an ordinary visible critique, with fewer endorsement flips driven by confidence or copied conclusions.

stages.instruction: Bind unchanged seed and public seam policy; reserve both calls including the worst-case second-input size.
Answer every requested part; attach the bounded DAG with explicit seam premises and conclusion fields. Do not pack conclusions into premise names or descriptive labels.

stages.role: Deterministic seam selection and field masking
stages.instruction: Validate DAG and choose up to four seams by fixed rule. Expose only whitelisted typed inputs and output types; exclude original conclusions, descendant text, confidence and identity. Freeze a visibility manifest. Empty or invalid DAG stops replay as incomplete, with unused reservation retained/reconciled normally.

Using the exact seed and masked capsules, reconstruct each requested seam output under its declared assumptions. Flag missing assumptions and unsupported interfaces; do not estimate the original author's likely answer.

Check scope-aware equivalence or exact counterexamples, retaining UNKNOWN when unavailable. Propagate original and reconstructed parent residuals to descendants. Render original full candidate with seam annotations; never replace a seam unless the complete dependency transport is checked. Freeze before separate evaluation.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Same two calls and allowances, with seam conclusions visible to the second call; all deterministic host checks unchanged.
ablations: Mask author/confidence only, leaving conclusions visible
Choose seams uniformly using a preregistered host seed instead of dependency influence
Replay every affordable seam without residual propagation
Replace the second call with deterministic checking alone
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Unrelated synthetic DAGs contain wrong conclusions, false shared premises, missing inputs and valid equivalent formulations. Measure seam fault discovery, false accusations and inherited-error propagation. On the fixed benchmark measure completeness and blinded trusted score after freezing; the four seams are not four independent experimental units.

nodes.falsification: The mechanism fails if masked replay does not improve fault localization over visible critique, if masking materially reduces completeness without benefit, or if any dependent conclusion is cleared despite a required unresolved parent. A copied hidden conclusion found in a visible field invalidates the blindness condition for that run.
risks: Premise choice and output type may reveal the candidate conclusion; blindness is limited and must be audited.
Both calls can reproduce the same erroneous rule or accept the same false premise.
Structural centrality may select easy steps while missing the important unsupported analytic bridge.
nodes.budget_formula: C_max <= 14000*p_in + 4700*p_out + sum(F_s) + R. At conditional ceilings and R=0.01, reserve USD 0.0475; output caps 2800 and 1900. Missing/invalid seams skip the second call; no replacement or repair call is allowed.

nodes.name: Predicate-scoped early exit with one reserved continuation

mathematical_basis.known_method: Finite-horizon stopping and explicit shared-fuel accounting.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Compile a fixed two-call graph with one host decision after a complete first response. Stop if all declared public predicates pass; continue only for an allowlisted repairable residual; otherwise stop unresolved. The stop reason is scoped predicate closure, never correctness or confidence.
mathematical_basis.rule: Let G be the finite frozen predicate set and r the host residual vector. Continue iff usage is settled, a second call is already reserved, r contains an allowlisted repairable failure, and no blocking infrastructure/unsupported condition holds. Otherwise freeze. All G passing proves only conjunction of G under its declared semantics; adequacy for the requested theorem remains separate.
mathematical_basis.termination: Number of dispatched calls N <= 2 by construction, independent of any real-valued progress score. Decreasing a heuristic residual is not used as a termination or correctness proof.

assumptions: Public predicates and repair classes are frozen independently of private answers.
At most 24 requested slots and 48 public checks; bounded checker time and artifact size are pinned before dispatch.
A closed public predicate set may miss mathematical errors; final score is independently evaluated.
Only completed responses with reconciled usage can reach the continuation gate; streaming cancellation cannot release budget.
nodes.hypothesis: Against an always-two-call same-model draft/repair arm, early exit lowers mean cost without decreasing mean final rubric score by more than a preregistered 2/100 noninferiority margin on repeated runs of this item. An inconclusive interval supports no advantage claim.

stages.instruction: Preserve seed bytes, freeze predicates and ordered requested slots, bind one run identity, and admit worst-case two-call cost using verified provider bounds. Refuse unsupported billing.

Address every requested slot using the unchanged seed. State assumptions, dependencies, and explicit unresolved cases. Supply only declared witness types; do not self-certify correctness or select a routing outcome.

Reconcile first-call usage. Run only public frozen checks. Stop on uncertainty, unsupported theories, or full declared-predicate closure. Continue once only for allowlisted repairable residuals, providing codes and artifact pointers without private diagnostic content.

Execute only on CONTINUE. With original seed unchanged, repair the named public residuals while preserving all requested slots. Retain unclosed obligations explicitly. No new attempts or task changes.

Join either the stopped draft or single continuation, replay applicable public checks, and freeze bytes and accounting. Exhausted repairs stay unresolved. Independent private review happens afterward and cannot reopen the run.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Always-two-call draft/repair with the same endpoint, total caps, checking rules, and seed.
ablations: One direct call with the combined output allowance
Continue after every public residual, without the repairability allowlist
Early exit on schema completion alone, explicitly a weak control
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Report call count and spend with raw rubric score, missing-slot count, unsupported assertion count, and stopping reason. Compare score differences and cost differences separately; no saving alone counts as success.

nodes.falsification: Falsify the noninferiority claim if the prespecified paired score interval excludes differences above -2 points; do not claim cost advantage if costs are not lower. Any lost requested slot, private-feedback routing, third call, or restart fuel reset falsifies the implementation contract.
risks: An incomplete public checker can stop an incorrect answer early.
A conservative unsupported-theory block can stop almost every run; report coverage and score.
Repair overhead may exceed savings or regress valid content.
The join must distinguish an intentionally skipped conditional stage from a missing response.
nodes.budget_formula: C_max <= 6000*p_in_1+2600*p_out_1+9000*p_in_2+1800*p_out_2+sum(F_s)+R. If each p_in<=USD0.000001/token, p_out<=USD0.000005/token, F_s=0 and R=0.01, reserve USD0.047 for the complete two-call path; early-exit path <=USD0.029. Refuse if verified input bounds exceed caps.

nodes.name: Public-residual cascade with independent escalation

mathematical_basis.known_method: A fixed model cascade with cost-sensitive routing, motivated by FrugalGPT.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Use a cheaper endpoint first and allow one predetermined higher-price endpoint only for a frozen public residual class. Escalation receives the immutable seed, requested-slot inventory, and public residual classes but not the cheap answer, reducing direct anchoring. It must produce a full replacement response; no unverified prose merge.
mathematical_basis.rule: For draft cost C_L, escalation cost C_H, and escalation indicator e, C=C_L+e*C_H. If e occurs with probability q over repeated provider samples, E[C]=E[C_L]+E[e*C_H]; replacing the second term by q times a constant is valid only for fixed C_H. This identity implies no accuracy ordering between endpoints.
mathematical_basis.selection: Final output is the cheap response when e=0 and the complete escalated response when e=1. Host predicates decide routing, not mathematical truth. Pricing tier is never evidence of higher correctness.

assumptions: Both endpoint identities, tariffs, settings, and the escalation-class table are frozen before any run; no adaptive arm change as results arrive.
Escalation classes arise solely from public candidate checks, such as missing required slots or malformed supported witnesses, and contain no expected formulas.
A higher-price endpoint may be worse; independent post-freeze evaluation is mandatory.
No statistical confidence calibration or difficulty predictor is learned from this seed's private results.
nodes.hypothesis: The registered cascade has lower mean cost than always using the escalation endpoint while its paired final rubric score stays within a preregistered 2-point noninferiority margin; compare also with cheap-only to quantify whether escalation adds measured value.

stages.instruction: Pin both endpoints and the residual routing table. Preserve exact seed message. Reserve the two-call maximum in one ledger, including all conditional fees; refuse if either endpoint lacks enforceable bounds.
Attempt all requested parts and mark unresolved parts. Provide declared public-check artifacts and assumptions. Do not predict your accuracy, choose escalation, or alter the seed.

Settle usage and run frozen public checks. Stop on uncertain accounting or infrastructure failure. Escalate once only if a frozen residual class matches; build a separate prompt with original seed, slot inventory, and allowlisted public class codes, excluding the cheap answer and private material.

Execute only when routed. Independently address the unchanged full request with explicit assumptions, derivation, and unresolved cases. Public residual class codes indicate checks to address, not known answers. Return a full answer within the cap.

Freeze the cheap answer on non-escalation or the complete replacement on escalation; no best-answer selection by private score and no cross-model blending. Keep both artifacts for later independent paired analysis. Refusal or truncation stays in the denominator.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Always-high endpoint with its matched permitted budget; cheap-only direct baseline is also required.
ablations: Same second call uses the cheap endpoint
Escalation receives the cheap response as well as public codes
Always escalate, with the same total path caps
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Measure escalation frequency, score gain conditional on escalation, overall score/cost, full-answer completeness, and regressions. Report equal-money and equal-token experiments separately; do not compare dissimilar budgets under a single efficiency label.

nodes.falsification: No supported advantage if cost saving is absent, final score falls beyond the registered margin, or confidence intervals remain inconclusive. A more expensive endpoint consistently reducing score refutes the proposed endpoint pair. Any fallback after uncertain usage or unregistered route is a contract violation.
risks: Residual classes may correlate poorly with actual mathematical difficulty.
Cheap-call overhead can make always-high cheaper on frequently escalated runs.
Removing the draft may lose useful work; providing it may cause anchoring, hence the ablation.
Routing conditioned on draft output creates selection bias; overall paired score and all-run denominator remain primary.

Conditional thresholds p_in_L<=0.000001, p_out_L<=0.000005, p_in_H<=0.000003, p_out_H<=0.000015 USD/token, F_s=0, R=0.01 yield USD0.0905 for both calls. This is a conditional envelope, not a live price quote or external billing guarantee.

nodes.name: One-call selective publication with explicit coverage

mathematical_basis.known_method: Selective prediction measures error among asserted outputs together with coverage, rather than rewarding abstention alone.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: After one model call, a frozen host policy maps every requested slot to ASSERTED_UNVERIFIED, PREDICATE_SUPPORTED, or UNRESOLVED. The strict experimental arm publishes only predicate-supported claim blocks and an explicit unresolved marker for every withheld slot; retain the full raw draft for offline scoring. No retry or hidden completion is allowed.
mathematical_basis.metrics: For n fixed requested slots across recorded runs, let g_i indicate a published answer and let loss_i be independently adjudicated error afterward. Coverage=sum(g_i)/n; selective_error=sum(g_i*loss_i)/sum(g_i), undefined when sum(g_i)=0. Also report full 100-point rubric scores with withheld slots unfulfilled. These empirical descriptors do not imply an IID distribution over physics problems or formal correctness.
mathematical_basis.premise_boundary: The host's publication gate uses public predicate receipts with explicit scope, never confidence, apparent reasoning length, cost, or private correctness labels. Predicate-supported remains weaker than globally correct.

assumptions: Requested slots are frozen independently of the candidate; they cannot be deleted to improve coverage.
Claim blocks have explicit slot/dependency bindings; a withheld premise forces dependent claims unresolved.
Frozen acceptance policies and any coverage target are registered before execution and not tuned using this seed's private scores.
Checker inadequacy and false rejection are evaluated on independent public synthetic fixtures before any model pilot.
nodes.hypothesis: At one-call cost, the strict publication policy lowers adjudicated error among asserted parts while retaining at least 80% of the raw draft's attempted-slot coverage; full rubric score loss and all abstentions remain visible. If the coverage target is unmet, no quality improvement is claimed from a lower conditional error alone.

stages.instruction: Keep the unchanged seed as its own message, fix the complete requested-slot inventory and public predicates, and reserve the single call. Refuse uncertain provider bounds or unsupported fees.

Address every requested slot, separating assumptions, dependencies, claim blocks, and permitted witnesses. Mark unsupported conclusions unresolved. Do not omit difficult parts or claim your confidence establishes correctness.

Reconcile cost; stop on uncertainty. Check only frozen public predicates, propagate withheld dependency status, and retain raw bytes. Publish each passing claim block with its actual predicate scope; insert UNRESOLVED for every other requested slot. Make no new mathematical claims and issue no second model call.

Freeze raw and selective outputs with the same run/cost provenance before independent review. Report coverage, score and error jointly; zero asserted answers makes selective error undefined, not zero. Any later tuning is exploratory and a different experiment.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Same frozen raw one-call draft evaluated alongside its selective rendering; paired transformation isolates publication effects without another provider sample.
ablations: Schema-only publication filter
No dependency propagation
Pre-registered permissive arm publishes unsupported claims explicitly as unverified
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Independent evaluator scores raw and selective outputs after freezing. Report error among published slots, slot coverage, full rubric score, false rejections, and unchanged provider cost. Pairing cannot establish broader population calibration.

nodes.falsification: Reject the proposed improvement if asserted error does not fall, if coverage is below 80% of raw attempted coverage, or if deletion creates a false impression of full completion. Any unsupported dependent claim surviving withheld premises falsifies the publication contract.
risks: Abstention can game selective error; coverage floor and full rubric score are required.
A narrow exact checker may withhold correct analytic arguments.
Granularity of requested slots affects metrics and must stay fixed.
Host rendering can accidentally change meaning; preserve claim bytes, scope annotations, and raw-output hashes.
nodes.budget_formula: C_max <=9000*p_in+4500*p_out+F+R. Conditional thresholds p_in<=USD0.000001/token, p_out<=USD0.000005/token, F=0, R=0.01 yield USD0.0415 for the complete one-call workflow. No paid judge or repair is included; a metered evaluator would require an additional explicit reservation.

nodes.name: Basis-orbit covariance with inverse and composition controls

mathematical_basis.known_method: Metamorphic testing by equivariance under a declared group action.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Obtain one original-task derivation with a restricted evaluable AST. The host evaluates candidate objects in the original coordinate context and in bounded checking views, instead of asking for new transformed tasks. Use exact permutation/phase transforms and rational orthogonal rotations; sample a pair g,h and check inverse and composed paths as well as individual relations. The second call may repair only original-answer claims named by failed public checks.
mathematical_basis.obligations: For an admitted unitary U, define T_U(X)=U X U^dagger and T_U(v)=U v, with every operator, state, and measurement transformed consistently. U^dagger U=I gives T_U(XY)=T_U(X)T_U(Y); trace cyclicity gives tr(T_U(X))=tr(X). A candidate function F is checked against F(T_U(x))=T_U(F(x)) only when its signature and an independently admitted covariance rule license that relation. T_V(T_U(X))=T_(VU)(X) and T_(U^dagger)(T_U(X))=X supply transform implementation controls. Scalar invariants use the trivial output action; vector/eigenvector outputs require phase/subspace equivalence, not raw equality.
mathematical_basis.bounded_checker_fragment: Exact finite matrix equality over a proposed complex-rational pair codec; current repository Q is rational only. Signed permutations and real rational rotations can first use the existing rational substrate. Symbolic or transcendental evaluation is unsupported unless an independently checked adapter is supplied. Numeric sampled covariance is labelled numerical evidence only.
mathematical_basis.nonvacuity: Never construct both sides by transforming the same output and call the equality a test of the candidate. Re-evaluate the candidate AST on transformed source objects on one path; transport its original result on the other. A formula that does not expose a meaningful equivariant input signature is OPEN. Zero and identity functions may pass all orbit relations while being wrong; independent public structural predicates and later private scoring remain necessary.

assumptions: The original source-object extraction is bound to exact public seed spans and reviewed public conventions; unverified extraction remains an explicit residual rather than a trusted solution.
Transform registries and action proofs are frozen before observing candidate responses. No model invents a symmetry of the physical task.

Only coordinate covariances with declared output actions are used. Entanglement claims require local unitaries relative to the unchanged subsystem partition; global basis changes cannot silently preserve a fixed tensor-factor interpretation.
The restricted AST contains no arbitrary code, filesystem access, dynamic tool invocation, or unbounded evaluation.
nodes.hypothesis: At equal two-call resources, independently evaluated orbit relations plus one bounded repair detect basis-order, missing-conjugation, and inconsistent-object transformations more effectively than generic consistency review, without reducing completion of the original requested derivation.

stages.role: PFP input binding and OPERADS context admission
stages.instruction: Preserve seed bytes and full prompt hashes. Freeze action registry, exact/numerical labels, EIS clean/mutant calibration panel, requested-sink inventory and total reservation. PCIV protects seed, original task contract and registry.

stages.role: Original derivation and evaluable claim proposer
stages.instruction: Answer the unchanged task, with source-bound objects and bounded AST claims. State basis, tensor partition and output action for each checkable claim. All seed-requested parts remain required. Do not invent a host verdict.

stages.role: Independent view evaluation and finite EIS screening
stages.instruction: Choose at most 8 transforms by a frozen answer-independent schedule; validate inverse/group-law controls and bridge premises. Evaluate candidate AST on transformed inputs separately from transport of outputs. Run calibrated detectors; emit only public failure class and affected claim IDs. Two correlated failures do not satisfy an independent EIS danger signal. Record PCIV view lineage without mutating seed.

Receive unchanged seed again. Repair named original-context claims or declare them unresolved. Never replace the task with a transformed view, remove requested parts, or silently change physical conventions. Only allowlisted artifact-local feedback is available.

Recompute affected checks under original bindings, retain remaining residuals, render the patched original answer deterministically and freeze before private scoring. Store cost and lineage; any early failure follows the same terminal recording policy without another call.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Same-model original derivation plus generic consistency review, identical total 4800 output-token cap and matched full input/cost accounting.
ablations: Individual orbit checks without inverse/composition controls
Transform the output on both paths, as an explicitly vacuous negative control
Context labels without source binding
Orbit screening without second-call repair
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: First calibrate EIS on unrelated exact synthetic matrices and deliberately corrupted basis/conjugation maps; include valid phases and degenerate subspaces. Measure mutant rejection, valid-control false rejection and uncovered AST claims. Then freeze paired benchmark outputs for independent scoring, reporting original-task completeness, accuracy, cost and failures. PCIV wrapper selection is offline on synthetic fixtures with fresh confirmation; never tune using the benchmark key.

nodes.falsification: A wrong conjugation, missing source transform, or mismatched inverse admitted as an exact covariance pass falsifies the checker contract. If zero/identity wrong functions receive a correctness label solely from equivariance, the semantic policy is falsified. No matched-budget improvement in convention-error detection or final completeness-adjusted accuracy falsifies the practical hypothesis.
risks: Covariant wrong functions are a large undetected family; orbit consistency is necessary only.
Shared parsing or source-extraction errors can corrupt both paths.
Sampling a small transform set covers neither all bases nor all symbolic parameters.
Eigenvector phase and degeneracy freedom cause false rejection unless subspace outputs are supported.
Token overhead may displace requested derivation content.
nodes.budget_formula: Full path bind->derive->orbit_check->repair->freeze: C_max <= 15000*p_in + (3300+1500)*p_out + F_1+F_2 + C_host_metered + R. With the common conditional thresholds, zero fees/metered host cost and R=0.01, reserve USD 0.049. Both model calls include the full unchanged seed; zero retries/fallback; refuse if actual input bounds or prices violate USD 0.10.

nodes.name: Quantity-covariant reparameterization with guarded limit squares

mathematical_basis.known_method: Quantity calculus, dimensional homogeneity, reversible changes of units, and conditional commutation of continuous maps with limits.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Type every expression by a dimension vector and keep physical quantities separate from numerical coordinates. Construct nonzero unit-rescaling views of the same objects. Separately test any candidate-asserted limit with an explicit continuity/domain witness; a limit is a consequence check, never an equivalent replacement task. The second call repairs dimensional or limit-bridge failures in the original answer.
mathematical_basis.obligations: If q=n*u and the basis units are changed by positive scales a_j, a quantity with dimension vector d has u'=a^d*u and n'=a^(-d)*n, where a^d=product_j a_j^(d_j). A numerical formula F of output dimension d_y must obey F(a^(-d_1)n_1,...)=a^(-d_y)F(n_1,...), with all dimensional constants transformed too. This follows from preserving each physical q. Sums require equal dimensions; products add dimension vectors; logarithms and exponentials require dimensionless arguments under the declared convention.
mathematical_basis.limit_bridge: For a public family x(epsilon) in a declared domain, x(epsilon)->x0 and continuity of an admitted map T at x0 imply lim T(x(epsilon))=T(x0). Record the domain, approach direction, topology, witness and applicable branch. A nonzero coordinate scaling is invertible; sending a scale to zero is not that same bridge. Taking a limit through an inverse requires invertibility near the limit; eigenvector branches or earliest-attainment functionals cannot inherit continuity from their input matrices. Unsupported continuity claims remain OPEN.
mathematical_basis.bounded_checker_fragment: Dimension vectors and positive rational scaling can be exact. A proposed rational-AST limit checker may cancel common polynomial factors only with a punctured-domain witness and retain a distinct extension value; substitution is valid only for denominators certified nonzero at the limit. General multivariate/transcendental or optimization limits require separately admitted proof rules. Finite numerical approach sequences are diagnostics, never certificates of existence or equality of limits.

assumptions: Dimension assignments follow explicit public conventions; a convention setting a physical constant to one must retain its original dimension metadata.
All positive unit scales are declared and reversible; no physically different coupling or boundary condition is substituted for the original task.
Limit probes are restricted to a preregistered public rule library and candidate-asserted families, without answer-key-selected limits.
Required original branches remain present even if a limiting branch is easier to check.
nodes.hypothesis: Combining exact dimensional checks with explicitly guarded limiting relations reduces missing-scale factors and unjustified boundary substitutions more efficiently than asking the model to check dimensions and special cases in prose.

stages.instruction: Keep original bytes as their own message. Freeze dimensions, permitted convention restoration, scaling schedule and limit-proof rules. OPERADS colours include dimension and branch context; PCIV protects them and the seed. Reserve both calls.

Answer the original task in its original conventions. Annotate candidate expressions with dimension vectors, branch guards and explicit limit claims. Do not assume a dimensionless numerical symbol means its physical quantity has no units.

Evaluate at most 8 positive rational unit changes and validate independent typed AST paths. For limits, check only admitted continuity/domain witnesses and label unsupported cases OPEN. EIS screens known dimensional/branch mutants with valid singular-looking controls. Record PCIV transformation lineage; never infer correctness from a vanishing diagnostic.

Receive the exact seed again. Repair affected original expressions, restore missing dimensional constants, or provide admitted domain/continuity evidence. Preserve every original requested branch and report unresolved obligations. No private evaluation feedback is available.

Recheck changed quantities and branches, deterministically render the original-context answer, and freeze all outputs before trusted scoring. Keep dimensional, exact-limit and numerical-limit evidence distinct; record missing parts and cost.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Two-call derivation and prose review explicitly mentioning dimensions and limiting cases, with identical 4400 total output-token cap.
ablations: Dimension typing alone
Numerical approach sequences without continuity certificates, labelled diagnostic-only
Scale checks without transforming dimensional constants
Limit checking without explicit branch/domain context
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Use unrelated synthetic quantity equations with incorrect exponents, missing constants, removable singularities, poles, branch switches and discontinuous attainment maps. Predeclare clean/mutant panels and report both false rejection and detection. Score frozen original benchmark answers separately; no feedback selects unit scales, limits or repairs. PCIV may select wrapper variations only on independent fixtures before the benchmark.

nodes.falsification: Reject a checker that treats zero scaling as an invertible unit change, accepts dimensionally inconsistent addition, or certifies a limit from finite numerical agreement alone. Reject the workflow advantage if matched-budget errors or completeness do not improve over prose review, or if valid convention choices are systematically rejected.
risks: Dimensionally correct expressions can have arbitrary incorrect dimensionless coefficients or signs.
Natural-unit conventions can hide dimensions unless metadata is explicit.
Limit existence and interchange are stronger claims than pointwise consistency.
Small-parameter examples may not probe the required exceptional branch.
A restrictive checker can leave most analytic work OPEN and consume scarce response tokens.
nodes.budget_formula: Full path bind->derive->check->repair->freeze: C_max <= 14000*p_in + (3000+1400)*p_out + F_1+F_2 + C_host_metered + R. At common conditional thresholds with zero extra charges and R=0.01, reserve USD 0.046. This includes both seeds, artifacts, all billable reasoning, failed calls and zero retries. Any excess estimate refuses dispatch.

nodes.name: Tensor-layout commuting squares with partition-sensitive detectors

mathematical_basis.known_method: Naturality of linear tensor operations under explicit coordinate maps, with direct index definitions as independent checking paths.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Represent candidate bipartite objects both as a labelled four-index tensor and a flat matrix. Check partial-trace and partial-transpose operations through separately implemented index and matrix paths. Use factor-order permutations and local unitary views to expose axis, conjugation and flattening errors; never infer entanglement facts merely from schema or orbit agreement.
mathematical_basis.obligations: Fix flat(i,alpha)=i*d_B+alpha. Define tr_B(X)_(i,j)=sum_alpha X_(i,alpha;j,alpha) and PT_B(X)_(i,alpha;j,beta)=X_(i,beta;j,alpha). Direct index substitution proves PT_B(PT_B(X))=X and tr_B(PT_B(X))=tr_B(X). For local U,V and X'=(U tensor V)X(U tensor V)^dagger, tr_B(X')=U tr_B(X)U^dagger and PT_B(X')=(U tensor conjugate(V))PT_B(X)(U tensor conjugate(V))^dagger. These are generic operator identities, not task answers.
mathematical_basis.bridge_proof: Prove each rule first on matrix units E_ij tensor E_ab, then extend by linearity. For partial trace, tr(V E_ab V^dagger)=tr(E_ab); for transpose, (V E_ab V^dagger)^T=conjugate(V) E_ba V^T. A factor-swap S maps X on A tensor B to S X S^dagger on B tensor A and must also relabel the traced/transposed subsystem. Verify flatten/unflatten inverses over all index positions. These proofs are declared mathematical bridges; machine-checked runtime correspondence remains a separate implementation obligation.
mathematical_basis.scope_rule: Arbitrary global unitaries do not preserve the fixed bipartition's reduction or partial-transpose invariants. PT is a linear map, not itself a unitary coordinate change, so only its commuting diagram under an admitted coordinate map is representation preserving. A PT positivity check is at most the predicate actually checked; no unrestricted separability conclusion is admitted. Involution and trace identities alone admit wrong functions, including identity-as-PT, so they cannot stand alone.

assumptions: Tensor dimensions, subsystem names, ordering and conjugation convention are explicit and bound to the public source object.
Exact controls include unequal subsystem dimensions and complex entries; real symmetric or maximally symmetric fixtures alone hide transpose mistakes.
The two computational paths do not call the same flattening or transpose helper; implementation diversity is recorded without claiming statistical independence.
Actual complex-rational pair arithmetic and typed tensor operations must be implemented; existing rational matrix port alone does not supply them.
nodes.hypothesis: At matched cost, commuting tensor-index paths with anti-vacuity controls catch subsystem and conjugation mistakes that basis-invariant scalar spot checks miss, while preserving the original full answer.

stages.role: PFP tensor-context binding and protected PCIV lineage
stages.instruction: Preserve immutable original seed and requested outputs. Freeze factor-label conventions and independently calibrated EIS fixtures. OPERADS colours carry factor order, dimensions and operation type. Reserve both model calls.

stages.role: Original derivation with labelled tensor artifacts
stages.instruction: Answer the original task and expose typed tensor/matrix objects and claimed operations. Retain the original subsystem interpretation. Flag unsupported extraction or analytic steps. Do not supply a transformed problem in place of the requested answer.

stages.role: Independent index/matrix checking and EIS controls
stages.instruction: Check all flatten/unflatten indices within bounds. Evaluate registered direct-index and separate matrix paths, local-unitary naturality and relabelled factor swaps. Use identity-as-PT, omitted conjugation, wrong traced axis and wrong flattening as answer-independent negative controls. Retain infrastructure failures separately. PCIV records each view and bridge lineage; no private data enters selection.

Receive unchanged seed again. Correct only implicated original-context tensor claims and downstream explanations or leave them OPEN. Keep the original partition, requested content and task conventions. Feedback contains public failure types and claim references only.

Recheck altered paths and dependants, deterministically produce the original answer, and freeze before private scoring. Label each check as exact instance, admitted identity, numerical or OPEN. Passing relations never produce an unqualified correct-answer label.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Two-call original derivation and generic tensor-convention review with the same endpoint, total 4800 output-token cap and full input reservation.
ablations: Only scalar trace and involution checks
Both paths sharing one indexing helper
Real equal-dimension fixtures only
Remove subsystem labels from operadic colours
Checks without bounded repair
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Calibrate against unrelated synthetic complex rational matrix units and valid density operators, with unequal-dimension cases and deliberately malformed axis maps. Measure path discrepancy detection, false rejection, identity-as-PT detection and unsupported rate. Compare frozen original-task correctness and completeness under matched budget; retain all failures. PCIV selects public fixture-tested wrapper changes offline, not via seed evaluator feedback.

nodes.falsification: If identity-as-PT or a wrong subsystem permutation passes the full calibrated detector panel, the proposed detector adequacy claim fails. Admission of an arbitrary entangling basis change as preserving fixed-partition invariants falsifies the bridge policy. No improvement over scalar checks/prose review at matched cost falsifies the workflow hypothesis.
risks: A wrong original state can satisfy every tensor identity.
Two implementations may share a conceptual indexing mistake despite separate code.
Highly symmetric fixtures conceal axis errors; calibration must include asymmetric controls.
A declared algebraic proof does not prove the compiled checker implements it.
Tensor annotations and repair feedback can reduce tokens available for the full derivation.
nodes.budget_formula: Full path bind->derive->square_check->repair->freeze: C_max <= 15000*p_in + (3300+1500)*p_out + F_1+F_2 + C_host_metered + R. Under common conditional thresholds, zero extra charges and R=0.01, reserve USD 0.049 for both calls together. Zero retries/fallback. Model outputs freeze even when a second stage cannot be admitted; failures remain in the denominator.

nodes.name: Two-axis checker assurance before evidence-guided repair

mathematical_basis.known_method: Mutation analysis of executable checkers, fault seeding in candidate artifacts, positive/negative controls and skeptical witness replay.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Cross artifact faults with checker faults rather than measuring only rejection of mutated answers. PFP supplies an exact declared relation and replay witness; PCIV records protected checker-policy mutation lineage; EIS admits only a checker that preserves clean controls and detects seeded bad controls; OPERADS prevents unchecked calibration output from being substituted for a checked receipt.
mathematical_basis.obligations: For synthetic labelled panel P={(x_i,y_i)} with y_i in {VALID,INVALID}, original checker V must agree with every required y_i. For executable non-equivalent checker mutants V_j, K_ij=1 exactly when V_j(x_i) differs from the reference label while V(x_i) agrees. Publish the full K matrix, clean rejection rate, faulty-artifact acceptance rate and mutant-kill rate. A crash or unsupported result has its own column and is not K_ij=1. Establish mutation non-equivalence by a separately replayed counterexample, otherwise retain UNKNOWN_EQUIVALENCE.
mathematical_basis.bounded_checker_fragment: Public small exact-rational linear identities, shape constraints and binding predicates only. Checker operators include inverted comparisons, omitted feasibility conjunct, stale binding acceptance, and skip-on-parse-error. Artifact faults are generated independently from checker operators and independently labelled by a small reference implementation. No transfer from this finite panel to analytic benchmark correctness is asserted.

assumptions: The synthetic relation and reference implementation are fixed before checker selection and do not import the mutated checker, its normalizer or private evaluator.
Development and confirmation fixture random seeds are sampled separately by the host; distinct seeds alone do not prove semantic or statistical independence of implementations.
A mandatory nonempty clean panel, nonempty invalid panel and constant-accept/constant-reject mutants prevent empty or constant success.
An independently implemented reference can still share a mistaken specification; this remains a stated assumption and risk.
nodes.hypothesis: At equal two-call money/token limits, the two-axis gate reduces false certification under injected checker faults relative to ordinary candidate-only mutation checks, without increasing rejection of supported clean artifacts by more than two percentage points on the preregistered synthetic confirmation panel.

stages.role: SeedBytes x CheckerBundle x MutationPlan -> FrozenRunContract
stages.instruction: Bind original seed bytes and reserve both calls. Freeze synthetic relation, reference, mutation operators, development fixtures and confirmation generation rule; no benchmark-key access.

Evaluate original and mutated checkers on independent synthetic controls. EIS screens the actual executable matcher against clean cases. Require mandatory constant-detector and omitted-predicate controls to be killed without treating exceptions as kills. Freeze chosen checker before confirmation; confirmation failure ends certification and triggers no in-run tuning. Failed preflight ends this branch with a noncertifying receipt and zero paid calls.
Produce the complete requested answer with explicit supported checkable artifacts and separate prose claims. Calibration establishes only finite control performance, not validity of your answer.

Replay only public supported predicates and bind every witness to candidate/checker hashes. Emit allowlisted failure classes and artifact pointers; a checker exception is infrastructure failure. Never consult key-derived expected values.

Use one bounded repair call on public witnessed findings only. Preserve the immutable seed and every requested part. Mark unsupported obligations open; checker disagreement does not authorize changing the task.
Recheck changed artifacts, propagate residuals and freeze response plus full ledger. Trusted private evaluation happens later with no return edge.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Same-model two-call draft/review, same 4200 total output cap and full-path reservation, with candidate-only controls and no checker mutation admission.
ablations: Remove checker mutations but keep clean and faulty artifact panels
Remove clean controls while retaining faulty artifacts
Count crashes as kills to expose misleading mutation scores
Use the checker itself as reference labels
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Preregister 64 clean and 64 invalid synthetic confirmation cases, at most 32 checker variants, operator/family strata and mandatory controls. Report raw paired outcomes, clean rejections, semantic misses, infrastructure failures and unknown equivalence separately. Compare final frozen benchmark scores only offline; no optimization or stopping based on the hidden key. A denominator of zero is undefined, not perfect performance.

nodes.falsification: Any constant checker admitted, omitted mandatory feasibility check surviving its dedicated counterexample, or exception counted as a semantic kill falsifies the assurance contract. No improvement in false certification on the fixed confirmation panel, or clean rejection rising beyond two percentage points, falsifies the practical hypothesis.
risks: A checker and reference may encode the same wrong relation.
A high score on hand-selected checker mutants may not predict genuine defects.
Calibration overhead may reduce answer completeness within the token cap.
Existing obstruction-branch runtime errors must be resolved or reported before claiming a completed calibration.
nodes.budget_formula: Full longest path: 14000*p_in + 4200*p_out + F_1+F_2+R, including both draft and repair, zero retries. At the stated conditional thresholds and zero F: USD 0.014+0.021+0.010=0.045 <=0.10. All calibration is bounded local computation; paid generation of controls is prohibited in this path.

nodes.name: Protected-distinction challenges for non-vacuous extractors

mathematical_basis.known_method: Positive/negative controls, observational equivalence and counterexample-guided specification testing.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Test the semantic information retained by an extractor before interpreting its obstruction score. Freeze independent synthetic valid/invalid pairs and require the extractor-detector composition to separate declared protected distinctions. PCIV mutates only extraction policies, EIS checks valid variants, PFP replays a label-changing witness, and OPERADS propagates UNSEPARATED_PAIR residuals into every dependent claim.
mathematical_basis.obligations: For extractor E:X->Z and detector D:Z->{PASS,FAIL,OPEN}, if E(x)=E(y) but public relation labels R(x) and R(y) differ, no deterministic D on Z alone can classify both correctly. Record this collision as an impossibility witness for that interface. Separately test nonconstant D on explicit valid/invalid controls; nonconstancy alone is necessary but insufficient. A zero value forced by d1*d0=0 on admitted inputs conveys no additional semantic distinction.
mathematical_basis.bounded_checker_fragment: Pairs from public synthetic trace families: copied input drift, omitted citation, unsupported-node deletion, changed value with unchanged well-formed shape, and a semantics-preserving reordering control. Validate whether each mutation actually changes the declared relation using an independently frozen reference; reject mislabeled mutations rather than counting them as detector misses.

assumptions: Protected distinctions are defined by public mathematical predicates rather than model confidence, key-derived labels or a desired score.
Equality of bounded extractor outputs is canonical and checked exactly; hashing alone is not a semantic equivalence proof.
A finite collision-free panel does not establish global injectivity or semantic adequacy.
The independent fault author/generator sees the public relation but is not driven by extractor implementation; source overlap is disclosed.
nodes.hypothesis: A frozen protected-distinction screen identifies semantic information loss that ordinary nonconstant-output controls miss, reducing false claims of certified correctness on untouched synthetic fault families at equal total model budget.

stages.instruction: Bind immutable seed and price reservation. Freeze the extractor, supported public relation, independently seeded development pairs, confirmation family inventory, and exact output codec. No seed-specific solutions are generated or supplied.

Replay both labels independently; check extractor equality and detector separation. Mandatory pairs include a semantically wrong admitted cochain case whose algebraic channel remains zero. Record structural admission and semantic relation separately. Reject global certification for any known collision; a failed required control ends this branch without paid calls. Freeze the candidate policy before confirmation and do not tune on confirmation results.

Produce the complete requested derivation with explicit assumptions and supported artifacts. Treat known blind spots as unverified obligations, not as permission to omit requested parts. Do not infer correctness from a zero diagnostic.

Evaluate only supported public relations. Every claim depending on a collision-prone projection inherits its unresolved distinction; preserve unparsed prose as unchecked. Emit public failure types and candidate-local witnesses only.
One bounded repair may add missing explicit artifacts or correct a publicly witnessed violation. It cannot modify the extractor policy, confirmation panel, seed or certification meaning.
Replay changed artifacts and retain unresolved collision scopes. Freeze final text before separate trusted evaluation; no private feedback edge exists.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Two-call draft/review with the same 4000 total output cap and an extractor checked only for valid syntax and nonconstant outputs.
ablations: Remove protected semantic pairs but retain constant-detector controls
Remove independent label replay
Drop unknown nodes during extraction
Use phi1=0 alone as a semantic acceptance criterion
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Use separate public development and confirmation families, not merely new random values of the same template. Publish pair-level labels, collision witnesses, separation outcomes, valid-control rejection and unsupported counts. Primary endpoint is false certification of relation-invalid synthetic artifacts; separately measure final-answer completeness and offline benchmark score. Repeated trials concern this fixed panel/item only.

nodes.falsification: A verified unequal-label/equal-extraction pair admitted as universally certified falsifies the scope contract immediately. If protected-distinction screening does not reduce false certification relative to nonconstant-only controls on the frozen family confirmation panel, the empirical hypothesis fails.
risks: Fault families may not represent mathematical reasoning failures.
Input drift may be invisible to both a detector and a shared reference parser.
Artificially adding distinguishing metadata can game the screen unless the detector consumes the intended semantic field.
A pairwise screen can still miss failures involving three or more interacting claims.
nodes.budget_formula: Full longest path: 12000*p_in + 4000*p_out + F_1+F_2+R. Conditional thresholds give USD 0.012+0.020+0.010=0.042, two calls, zero retries. Separate synthetic controls are host-generated with no paid calibration call; unknown additional cost refuses dispatch.

nodes.name: Compositional fault propagation with receipt-level canaries

mathematical_basis.known_method: End-to-end fault injection, dependency tracking, fail-closed validation and controlled component substitution.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Mutate public synthetic artifacts at typed edges, then also mutate checker receipts and routing operations to test whether local detections survive workflow composition. PFP binds witnesses to exact artifacts, PCIV preserves mutation lineage, EIS calibrates valid-control behavior, and OPERADS requires unresolved parent effects to persist into final outputs. A one-call answer path consumes this separately calibrated pipeline.
mathematical_basis.obligations: For DAG G, required dependency edge u->v propagates unresolved residuals: U(v) contains U(u) unless a checked repair discharges the specific obligation under new artifact hashes. An injected fault is detected only when a replayable finding reaches every required dependent sink or the sink becomes OPEN. A local red verdict erased downstream is an end-to-end miss. For detector-stage j and injected fault i record B_ij in {DETECTED,PASS,OPEN,ERROR}; measure sink escape, not merely any local red.
mathematical_basis.bounded_checker_fragment: Synthetic pipelines of at most 64 nodes with exact-rational identities and host-owned receipt fields. Faults include stale parent hash, bypassed checker edge, invalid receipt substitution of the same type, dropped residual, incompatible codec interpretation, duplicated correlated signal and two cancelling intermediate value faults. A final true relation with a false intermediate claimed step is labelled by the declared proof-trace property, separately from final-value correctness.

assumptions: The trusted host scheduler, receipt signature/binding code and mutation harness are outside the mutated boundary; this trust boundary is explicit rather than inferred from types.
The independent host health signal is a replayed control failure or custody failure, not a second paraphrase of model agreement.
Compound mutation labels are independently replayed; cancelling output errors are not automatically labelled wrong final answers.
Confirmation fault locations and random seeds are committed after the pipeline is frozen, with no access to benchmark evaluation feedback.
nodes.hypothesis: On a fixed confirmation panel, receipt-level canaries reduce the fraction of injected faults escaping to certified dependent sinks relative to local-only checking, including same-type component substitutions and cancelling faults, while all supported clean controls remain accepted.

stages.instruction: Bind original seed bytes, frozen DAG, public synthetic relation, mutation/custody policy and one-call ledger. Protect seed, budget and reference labels from PCIV mutation.

In isolated local copies inject fixed artifact, receipt and routing faults. Run clean controls and separately authored compound cases; calculate which required sinks remain certified. Exercise same-type substitution, stale hashes, residual deletion and correlated-signal duplication. Exceptions and timeouts remain ERROR, not successful detection.

Require no escape for mandatory fault controls and no rejection of supported clean controls. Freeze pipeline before independent confirmation; failure ends this branch with zero paid calls and no in-run retuning. Admission says only that the finite panel passed.

Produce the full requested answer with explicit dependency IDs and separately checkable public artifacts. Do not claim that synthetic canary success certifies the mathematical answer. No additional model checker or calibration call is allowed.

Check supported predicates, replay receipt bindings and propagate unresolved parent effects. Require a verified discharge before clearing a residual. Unsupported prose and theories remain unchecked. EIS may record a finding without an independent danger signal; it cannot invent a second signal to force a suppression label.
Freeze complete answer text with scoped checking receipts, residuals and ledger. No retry or model repair. Trusted benchmark evaluation occurs after this terminal stage without a return edge.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Same-model single-call response with 4000 output tokens and local checks, lacking end-to-end residual/receipt propagation.
ablations: Typed ports without replayed semantic receipts
Single faults only, omitting independently labelled compound faults
Any local red counts as end-to-end success
Allow receipt reuse after parent hash changes
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Preregister up to 128 synthetic cases per panel and distinguish final-value validity from proof-trace validity. Publish local and sink-level detection matrices, supported clean-control acceptance, infrastructure failures, false scope strengthening and host time. Separate configuration selection on development panels from untouched family/location confirmation. Benchmark scoring is a later frozen-output comparison only; no key-guided canaries.

nodes.falsification: Any required corrupted dependency whose sink retains a stronger certified scope without a checked discharge falsifies propagation. A same-type but invalid receipt admitted after substitution falsifies the host contract. No reduced sink escape rate or loss of clean-control acceptance falsifies the practical hypothesis.
risks: The scheduler or receipt verifier can be a common-mode single point of failure.
Real semantic dependency extraction may omit a premise despite perfect receipt propagation.
Fault injection can overstate robustness if only easy edges are selected.
Rejecting a proof trace with a coincidentally correct final value is valid only when the declared target includes trace validity; reports must keep both labels.
nodes.budget_formula: Full path: 9000*p_in + 4000*p_out + F_1+R = USD 0.009+0.020+0.010=0.039 at conditional thresholds. One paid model call, no paid checker/calibration model and zero retries. Include any metered host charge in R before admission.

nodes.name: Randomized second-slot repair versus independent re-derivation

mathematical_basis.known_method: Randomized treatment allocation conditional on a pretreatment stratum, followed by intention-to-treat estimation.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Generate one complete compact derivation, freeze it, and classify its public-check residuals. Within each fixed stratum, allocate the only remaining model slot to either repair of that artifact or a fresh complete derivation that cannot see it. The output cap, model/provider and monetary allowance are identical for the two actions. Thus the experiment identifies the value of allocating the second slot to an informed repair rather than another sample, instead of confounding an elaborate workflow with more model calls.
mathematical_basis.allocation: H=h(C1) belongs to {actionable_public_failure, unsupported_or_no_failure}; h and fixtures are fixed before any seed execution. Z~Bernoulli(1/2) is revealed after C1 and H are frozen. Z=1 supplies C1 plus only approved public failure codes; Z=0 supplies the seed and a frozen PCIV wrapper variant, but not C1. Both slot-two roles return a complete answer. A pre-generated blocked allocation table prevents outcome-responsive scheduling.
mathematical_basis.estimand: For final normalized rubric outcome Y(z) in [0,1], tau=E[Y(1)-Y(0)] over repeated calls on this fixed seed. With randomized positivity, no interference and consistent execution, tau_hat=N^-1 sum_i[Z_i*Y_i/0.5-(1-Z_i)*Y_i/0.5] is unbiased for that assigned-population contrast. Stratified mean differences may improve precision. The allocation estimator's summand has range [-2,2], so it needs its own valid randomization interval or Hoeffding radius sqrt(8*log(2*K/alpha)/N); do not reuse the paired-difference radius without adjustment.
mathematical_basis.selection: Use the same host selector in both arms: among complete schema-valid candidates, prefer fewer demonstrated public-predicate violations, then fewer unresolved required fields, then the lower fixed slot ID. Emit the chosen original answer unchanged with a receipt. No model self-score or private rubric appears in selection. If no complete candidate is usable, freeze an explicit partial/abstention with preserved artifacts.

assumptions: Random assignment is generated independently of provider outcomes and private evaluation; service conditions are blocked by nearby execution time and the endpoint is pinned.
Public checks identify only their declared predicates. A detector stratum can be uninformative about mathematical error and is never a correctness label.
Second-slot repair and fresh-generation bodies obey their typed information boundary. A fresh answer cannot retrieve the first response through shared conversation history.
The local selection rule and all wrapper variants are frozen on answer-independent fixtures; fresh draws are not assumed statistically independent merely because prompts differ.
nodes.hypothesis: At equal second-slot allowance, repair improves unconditional mean rubric score by at least 3 points over fresh re-derivation in the actionable-public-failure stratum; the overall contrast and other stratum are separately preregistered secondary outcomes.

stages.instruction: Verify exact seed inclusion, type-check the OPERADS composition, reserve aggregate maxima and freeze the PCIV wrapper lineage. Prepare concealed randomized second-role assignment. Preflight refusal is a recorded assigned-run outcome.

Receive unchanged seed in its own message. Produce a complete compact derivation with explicit claim IDs, assumptions, requested-part coverage and public-check artifacts; identify open obligations. Return at most 2200 billable output/reasoning tokens under the admitted endpoint semantics.

Freeze C1, run PFP public checks and calibrated EIS screening, determine the fixed stratum, then reveal the randomized role. Bind h, Z, propensity and all input hashes. RepairInput contains C1 and bounded non-secret failure codes; FreshInput contains no C1. Never pass a raw private/evaluator diagnostic.

One mutually exclusive paid operation, not two branches dispatched: repair C1 if assigned RepairInput; independently derive a complete answer if assigned FreshInput. Both receive the exact seed and the same 2200-token ceiling. If the first call has uncertain billing or the remaining reservation fails, issue SKIPPED without a provider call.

Recheck candidate artifacts, apply the fixed public selector, retain failures and both original outputs, freeze final bytes and ledger. The private evaluator later sees frozen candidates/final output only after the full campaign closes; its results cannot reopen this DAG.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Direct same-model single call with the same assigned money or token allowance in its respective panel; also a two-call draft plus generic self-critique control isolates extra-call effects.
ablations: Replace detector-stratified allocation with unstratified randomized allocation
Repair with generic feedback instead of public failure codes
Select slot two unconditionally instead of the fixed public selector
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Freeze N, strata, primary contrast and K first. Report arm/stratum assignment counts, delivered-answer score, all-run score, slot-two improvement over frozen C1, actual cost, token fields, wall latency, serialtime_proxy and missingness. First-draft scores are computed only in delayed private evaluation. Randomize run order within complete blocks; common timestamps or provider seed labels do not create paired counterfactuals.

nodes.falsification: The 3-point actionable-stratum advantage is contradicted when its multiplicity-adjusted upper confidence bound is below 3; a nonpositive upper bound rejects even a positive gain. Wide bounds mean inconclusive. Any second-role dispatch seeing a hidden score or a supposedly fresh branch seeing C1 falsifies the isolation contract.
risks: Thin strata and a tiny paid campaign may make the randomized contrast extremely imprecise.
Provider changes, cache carryover or rate-limit interference can invalidate stable-mean assumptions; record and block rather than pool silently.
A public selector can reject a correct but unfamiliar derivation or favor formally neat nonsense; rubric score remains the endpoint.
Testing many strata, allocation probabilities or selector tie-breaks after seeing grades creates multiplicity and same-item tuning.
nodes.budget_formula: At most two calls. Cmax<=16000*p_in+4400*p_out+F1+F2+R. At the stated conditional price ceilings and R=0.010, Cmax<=USD 0.048. Slot-two alternative roles share one reservation; they are never both executed. Actual cost is measured separately.

nodes.name: Public-evidence continuation gate with explicit abstention accounting

mathematical_basis.known_method: Selective prediction with a reject option and a bounded two-stage cascade.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Run one complete derivation and a public obligation audit. Spend the second call only when a fixed predicate finds a repairable public defect and a safe reservation remains. Stop with the first answer when no such defect is found; stop with explicit unresolved claims or abstention when infrastructure failure or unsupported obligations cannot be repaired by the admitted second-stage operation. No high self-confidence threshold or private expected-answer signal is used.
mathematical_basis.policy: g(C1,receipt) in {STOP_WITH_UNCHECKED_ANSWER,REPAIR_ONCE,PARTIAL_OR_ABSTAIN}. REPAIR_ONCE requires at least one declared repairable schema/identity/coverage defect, healthy bound checker, known billing and sufficient reservation. Unsupported analytic obligations remain OPEN rather than being treated as false. A direct host integrity refusal is enforced even without both EIS danger signals; immune suppression must not manufacture a second independent signal from the same model statement.
mathematical_basis.metrics: Let A=1 only for a delivered output labeled full_answer; partial answers and full abstentions have A=0 for this selective metric. For normalized trusted score Y, coverage=E[A], selective risk=E[A*(1-Y)]/E[A] when E[A]>0, and full-answer delivered utility=E[A*Y]. This strict utility gives partial answers zero while their independently graded raw rubric score is still reported; the label full_answer asserts intended coverage, not correctness. Preserve the original unfiltered final rubric score too, including partial answers. Score-based risk is rubric loss, not the probability that every formula is correct; report the separately defined complete-correctness indicator if the evaluator supports it. C=C1+1{REPAIR_ONCE}*C2 and E[C]=E[C1]+E[1{REPAIR_ONCE}*C2]; factorization is not assumed.
mathematical_basis.stopping: All stopping happens from frozen public rules before private grading. Campaign N is fixed. A later confidence interval is descriptive or fixed-N inference under its stated assumptions, not permission to stop early when a convenient significance level appears.

assumptions: A fixed public registry distinguishes demonstrated errors from absent evidence and unsupported theories.
EIS negative-selection fixtures and false-rejection controls are answer-independent, versioned and disjoint from any fixtures used to choose detector thresholds.
The public repair packet cannot expose expected corrections from private evaluation; PCIV only mutates the allowed wrapper/repair instructions while preserving seed bytes.
An early accepted result is merely an unchecked answer with bounded public evidence. Neither coverage nor zero public defects certifies the complete derivation.
nodes.hypothesis: Relative to always-repair two-call execution, the gate reduces mean realized provider spend by at least 15% while losing no more than 3 points in unconditional mean rubric score; both conditions must hold with the preregistered uncertainty treatment.

stages.instruction: Pin seed bytes, wrappers, detector controls, typed branch operations and both potential call ceilings. Validate finite host limits and fail closed on uncertain pricing. Do not run the seed to tune thresholds.

Produce a complete answer to every seed request with a compact claim/assumption map and explicit unresolved obligations. Seed remains a separate exact-byte message. The admitted completion cap is 2600 tokens including billable reasoning where applicable.

Freeze C1, invoke PFP public checks and EIS fixture-bound rules, then apply the preregistered decision table. STOP means no flagged repairable defect, not proven correctness. A budget or infrastructure issue yields an explicit partial/abstention outcome; missing mathematical support stays OPEN. Record the counterfactual rule conditions without private labels.

Dispatch only on Repair and known settled prior billing, with unchanged seed plus the public artifact and bounded defect codes. Return a 1600-token bounded patch or explicit inability. No automatic retry. Patches cannot alter seed assumptions or erase unsupported obligations. Non-Repair branches produce a host Skipped token and incur no call.

Apply only well-formed patches linked to declared claims, replay affected public checks, and preserve the original response. If patch verification fails, keep the original with unresolved status rather than inventing a successful repair. Freeze final bytes, coverage, statuses and cost receipt. Close every branch before separate private grading.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Direct same-model call at matched assigned money/token allowance, and always-repair using exactly the same draft/patch prompts and ceilings; the latter is the primary cost-saving comparator.
ablations: Randomly skip the second slot at a preregistered fixed probability, separating detector value from generic economizing
Always deliver the first artifact without selective status
Use single-signal detector matches for continuation only, preserving direct host integrity refusals
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Report unconditional raw rubric score, operational delivered utility, abstention and partial rates, score-loss coverage curve at the one preregistered gate, actual spend and both time metrics. Selected-answer accuracy is secondary. Validate the gate using synthetic valid/invalid receipts including missing usage, checker exception, exact contradiction and unsupported expression. Retain all assigned failures; grade missingness gets bounds. Any extra gate thresholds are exploratory or increase K.

nodes.falsification: Reject the declared savings/noninferiority conjunction if either the upper confidence bound on savings is below 15% or the upper confidence bound on the score difference is below -3 points; intervals crossing the thresholds are inconclusive. Any path labeling unsupported mathematics as certified or hiding abstentions from the denominator falsifies the mechanism contract.
risks: Reducing coverage alone can improve accepted-only accuracy, so that metric cannot establish benefit.
The gate might spend more often on intrinsically difficult outputs; naive repaired-versus-unrepaired comparisons are confounded and are not causal evidence.
Public fixed thresholds can be overfit to the same seed after viewing grades; no within-campaign changes are permitted.
A short patch can leave stale downstream dependencies; replay is required and residuals remain visible.
nodes.budget_formula: Cmax<=15000*p_in+4200*p_out+F1+F2+R<=USD 0.046 at the conditional ceilings. Actual cost equals the first-call bill plus a second-call bill only when dispatched, plus priced fees. Reserve for the worst branch before admission; unused capacity is a measured saving, never an automatic extra retry.

nodes.name: Deadline-frozen two-candidate portfolio with serial and parallel schedules

mathematical_basis.known_method: Bounded algorithm portfolios, fork/join scheduling and performance profiles under a fixed deadline.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Create two complete candidate attempts with fixed PCIV wrapper variants, neither seeing the other, and compare parallel dispatch with serial dispatch using the same two-call allowance and public selector. At a preregistered deadline, freeze a usable completed candidate or abstain. This directly measures whether concurrency buys delivery latency on the fixed seed without pretending it reduces total provider work or cost.
mathematical_basis.time_model: Let dj be each observed dispatch-to-terminal duration and h total host overhead. Without queue contention, parallel wall latency is approximately h+max(d1,d2), serial wall latency approximately h+d1+d2; serialtime_proxy=d1+d2 in both schedules. Actual timestamps, concurrency contention and transport time override this approximation. Provider-reported compute time, if absent, is unavailable rather than inferred.
mathematical_basis.deadline_rule: D is fixed before dispatch and measured from run admission. At D choose only schema-usable candidates whose full bytes arrived and public checks completed by D using the same fixed selector; deterministic slot ID breaks ties. No usable candidate yields abstention. Late results are retained for accounting and a clearly separate offline sensitivity analysis, never substituted into the frozen primary result. Client cancellation does not release an uncertain billing reservation.
mathematical_basis.resource_rule: Use two predeclared full-answer variants with 2200-token ceilings; no extra synthesis/judge call. The serial comparator starts slot 2 only if policy permits before D, with an undisbursed reservation otherwise unused. Keep assigned two-slot allowance fixed and compare actual dispatch/cost separately. A second no-deadline paired panel isolates scheduling overhead from deadline censoring.

assumptions: The provider permits the declared concurrency and documents charge/token caps. Concurrency itself may induce queueing or rate limits, which are measured rather than assumed absent.
Both PCIV wrapper variants preserve the full immutable seed and are fixed before execution; no specialized seed subproblem or derived formula is substituted.
The final selector uses only PFP/EIS public receipts and slot IDs. It does not select by a private score, model self-confidence, or answer agreement.
A strict wall deadline includes bounded host validation time; the adapter must reserve time to freeze a result and label any missed deadline explicitly.
nodes.hypothesis: At equal monetary and output-token allowance, parallel scheduling increases the fraction of assigned runs delivering a candidate by the fixed deadline, with at most a 3-point reduction in unconditional mean rubric score; any latency advantage must be reported alongside unchanged or higher actual aggregate spend and serialtime_proxy.

stages.instruction: Create two typed operations from protected PCIV wrapper variants. Randomize schedule/run order within preregistered blocks. Reserve both worst-case calls transactionally before parallel dispatch; set an absolute deadline and a fixed host-check margin. No private feedback is available.

Receive the entire unchanged seed and variant A. Return a complete compact derivation with claim IDs and explicit open obligations, at most 2200 billable output/reasoning tokens. No access to B, filesystem, retrieval or evaluator. Execute when the scheduler assigns slot A; scheduler order is an explicit resource constraint rather than a data dependency.

Receive the entire unchanged seed and variant B, never A's output. Use the same 2200-token ceiling. Parallel mode starts both ready operations; serial mode permits only one active call and randomizes which slot goes first. If the deadline or uncertain billing forbids dispatch, return NotDispatched with no provider request.

Treat every dependency as a total terminal result including PendingAtDeadline, not an instruction to wait forever for both providers. Apply bounded PFP/EIS checks to arrived candidates, choose via the fixed selector, and retain detector/control receipts. OPERADS type compatibility alone does not validate this deadline semantics; the scheduler adapter needs synthetic event-trace tests.

Freeze chosen bytes or abstention no later than the admitted deadline, recording a miss if overhead exceeds it. Late provider settlement is append-only accounting outside the answer-producing DAG; never change selected bytes. All charged or uncertain work remains in the aggregate ledger and denominator. Private grading begins only after campaign output freeze.

baseline_and_ablations.baseline: Direct same-model one-call answer with matching assigned total monetary/token allowance, plus serial execution of the identical two candidate operations as the primary scheduling comparator.
ablations: Parallel candidates with identical wrappers, isolating diversity from scheduling
Choose the fixed first usable slot instead of ranking public receipts
No-deadline execution of both schedules, keeping both calls and reporting complete-run latency separately
baseline_and_ablations.evaluation: Use a fixed deadline chosen from infrastructure-only timing pilots or a user latency requirement, never from private seed scores. Report deadline-delivery fraction over all assigned runs, unconditional rubric score, abstention, per-slot error/rate-limit counts, actual tokens/costs, critical-path wall latency and sum of observed call durations. Completed-by-deadline results are the primary endpoint; survivor-only latency summaries and late-result scoring are secondary and explicitly labeled. Shared endpoint contention means paired blocks need workload isolation or a descriptive caveat.

nodes.falsification: A simultaneous upper confidence bound at or below zero for the deadline-delivery improvement rejects a positive scheduling benefit. A score-difference upper bound below -3 points rejects the noninferiority requirement. A late candidate replacing the frozen answer, a third model call, or a cancellation treated as zero cost falsifies the implementation contract.
risks: Parallel calls can worsen queueing, throttle each other or multiply timeouts; shorter theoretical critical path is not observed benefit.
Selecting among completed candidates creates completion-time selection bias; keep late, failed and undispatched slots visible.
Polling/stream parsing overhead can miss the wall deadline even if the provider completed earlier.
Changing wrapper diversity, schedule and selector simultaneously confounds mechanisms; retain the serial identical-body control and fixed ablations.
nodes.budget_formula: Two calls maximum. Cmax<=12000*p_in+4400*p_out+F1+F2+R<=USD 0.044 at the conditional ceilings. Parallel dispatch holds both reservations before any request. Deadline expiry never refunds an uncertain call. Serial and parallel have equal assigned limits; actual realized costs may differ because the serial second slot can remain undispatched.

nodes.name: Information-flow certificates that preserve blind stages under composition

mathematical_basis.known_method: Information-flow typing, provenance propagation and relational noninterference tests.
mathematical_basis.proposed_adaptation: Compile each stage's declared visibility into an origin-set effect alongside its mathematical port type. PFP binds the exact materialized request to a contract; PCIV records wrapper and broker transformations; EIS screens the compiler with benign and deliberately leaking synthetic controls; OPERADS rejects substitutions whose information effects exceed the recipient's allowed view. Demonstrate it on a complete solver followed by a candidate-blind challenge call, while keeping the challenge input independent of the solver output.
mathematical_basis.rule: For a node v, L(v) contains its direct data origins plus all data and control-dependency origins. In a DAG compute the union in topological order, or reach a fixed point. A request for blind role b is allowed only if L(request_b) is a subset of Allowed(b). Candidate presence, candidate-derived IDs/hashes, exception strings, token counts and dispatch decisions are origins too. Merely renaming or hashing a field does not declassify it.
mathematical_basis.relational_obligation: For deterministic request compiler K, synthetic hidden inputs h,h' and identical public p and randomness r, require Observe_b(K(p,h,r)) = Observe_b(K(p,h',r)). Observe includes exact message bytes, tools, model/settings, budget allowance, dispatch flag and routing metadata. Challenges must be scheduled independently of candidate content. Finite twin probes falsify leaks but do not prove noninterference for arbitrary code. Real provider timing/cache channels are outside this bounded claim and recorded as residual.
mathematical_basis.system_bridge: A compiler receipt names the pinned request builder and field-level origin derivation. That receipt is consumed by the broker before dispatch; a separate synthetic mutation panel challenges the same builder, not a textual copy. Lineage-only OR taint is insufficient because wrapper choice can leak via control flow.
mathematical_basis.distinct_from_prior: R05-I02 proposes candidate-blind challenge generation, and R08-I03 tests fault propagation. This proposal tests whether that blindness survives composition, including implicit channels and a correct-colour but wrong-visibility substitution. It does not claim a new challenge strategy or that two same-model calls have independent errors.
mathematical_basis.external_signature: (RunContext, VisibilityContract, SyntheticLeakPanel, PinnedRequestBuilder) -> OutcomeWithVisibilityReceipt. RunContext -> Outcome is valid only after the three external bundles are independently supplied and frozen; no prior candidate Outcome can supply a clean calibration panel or retroactively authorize visibility.
mathematical_basis.native_lowering: Use a serial product packet with a host-only sealed candidate and separately materialized model views. Passing a host packet down one edge is not permission to serialize all its fields into the model. No implicit native fan-out or coercion from candidate-sealed to candidate-visible ports.

assumptions: The trusted broker has no private answer key, private evaluator route, filesystem/repository retrieval or model conversation history beyond the explicitly constructed messages.
